headline: House resolution, which was tabled, would have required the Ethics Committee to keep and publicly release records on sexual misconduct cases involving members.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the House Ethics Committee to preserve all records, including investigative materials, about violations or alleged violations of House rules involving sexual harassment, unwelcome sexual advances, or sexual assault by House members. Within 60 days of adoption, the committee would have had to publicly release available reports, conclusions, recommendations, exhibits, and attachments from those investigations. Names and other identifying information of victims, alleged victims, and witnesses would have been blacked out.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House, Delegates, and the Resident Commissioner
who_it_affects.how: Ethics Committee records about sexual misconduct claims against them would have been kept and made public.

who_it_affects.group: Victims, alleged victims, and witnesses in House ethics cases
who_it_affects.how: Their personal identifying information would have been removed from any records released to the public.
It would have been required to preserve these records and publish them within 60 days.
People would have gained access to reports and findings from these House ethics investigations.
